C1 establishes book and author. C3 establishes a journal article by Alka Marwaha, topic similar, published in 2022. That seems to directly satisfy obligation? C3 provides article title, journal, year, volume, issue, pages. It is by Alka Marwaha. Topic similar? The title mentions "mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation" — similar to Vipassana and Mathematics. Published 2022, which is six years after 2016. So likely supported by C3 and C1. Maybe C1 needed to establish book date/topic. C3 supports article. Is there any missing? Possibly need confirm exact publication date six years after Nov 15 2016? C3 only year 2022. But "six years after that book" could be interpreted as year 2022. If exact date required, missing exact publication date. Does that sufficiently support? It supports publication in 2022, which is six calendar years after 2016. But not exactly six years to the day. Should we consider missing? The rules: "A Verified Claim supports only the entity, event, relation, role, date, quantity, and scope that it actually states. Do not transfer a date or property from one object to another. Do not strengthen a Claim." C3 states published in 2022. It does not state "six years after book". But from C1 book date 2016 and C3 article year 2022, we can infer six years in terms of year difference? The rule says don't strengthen. But simple arithmetic from stated dates? It says do not transfer date. We can compute? The evidence gap asks if claims support relevant parts. The obligation requires article published six years after. C3 gives year 2022. C1 gives book year 2016. That is a six-year difference in years. It may be sufficient to say published six years after (in year terms). But if strict exact date, missing exact publication date. The Local Obligation likely designed to find that article; C3 is likely the target. So maybe no missing. However, check: C3 article topic: "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation." Similar to "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics"? Yes, similar. C3 is a journal article. Published in International Journal of Statistics and Applied Mathematics. So it satisfies "journal article by Alka Marwaha on a topic similar to her book". Published in 2022, six years after 2016. So sufficient.

But wait: The obligation says "Establish and identify a journal article by Alka Marwaha ... published six years after that book, including whether such an article exists." C3 establishes existence. So supported_by C1, C3. C2 irrelevant. Missing null. Evidence_needed null.

However, let's consider if there is any nuance: The book is "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics" published November 15, 2016. Six years after would be 2022. C3 article published in 2022. It seems exactly the target. So no gap.

But maybe the obligation is to establish an article "on a topic similar to her book" and "published six years after that book". C3 article title mentions Vipassana and mathematics, similar. The date: C3 says published in 2022. That is six years after 2016. But if book published Nov 15, 2016, then six years after is Nov 15, 2022. C3 only gives year 2022, not month/day. Is that insufficient to establish "published six years after" exactly? The phrase "six years after" could mean in the year 2022. In common parlance, an article published in 2022 is six years after a book published in 2016. It's not exact to the day, but likely acceptable. The rules say don't strengthen. But we are not strengthening; we are comparing. The claim states 2022. The book date 2016. The difference is 6 years. So it's supported.

Could there be another missing element: "journal article by Alka Marwaha" — C3 says authored article. Yes. "on a topic similar to her book" — C3 title indicates mathematical overlaps of axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation. Book explores singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Similar.
